newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc hit by Centeon recall.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc hit by Centeon recall.

text.p: French chemical and pharmaceuticals group Rhone-Poulenc SA reported a 6.5 percent rise in first quarter net income on Wednesday and showed the scars of a costly Centeon product recall.

Rhone-Poulenc said the increase in net income would have been nearly 30 percent if not for the blood plasma product recall by the Centeon joint-venture in the U.S. between Rhone-Poulenc Rorer and Germany's Hoechst.
The first quarter net income rose to 674 million francs ($115.9 million) from 633 million on 2.2 percent higher sales at 21.6 billion francs.
On a comparable basis, taking account of sales and acquisitions, sales would have been up 6.3 percent.
Chairman and chief executive Jean-Rene Fourtou said that new products were fuelling earnings and made him confident of the company's profit aim despite Centeon.
"The new products launched in the life sciences businesses are contributing more and more significantly to the Group's results," he said.

"This is why we are maintaining our objective of increasing earnings per shares in 1997 by 20 percent, excluding exceptional items, and objective which is becoming more difficult because of the effect of Centeon," he added.
Such new products are the Taxotere anti-cancer drug, the Nasacort asthma drug, the Rilutek for the treatment of moto-neuron diseases and the Tripedia vaccine.

Operating income showed a 18.8 percent rise on a comparable basis to two billion francs. This reflected a big rise in pharmaceuticals and a small improvement and Fibers and Polymers as well as in animal health while the chemicals division showed a decline.
The chemicals division remained influenced by continued depressed titanium dioxide markets and increased prices of some raw materials.
Fibers and Polymers showed an increase despite a depressed polyester market, especially in Brazil.
A company spokeswoman said that manufacturing at Centeon had still not resumed but was expected to do so soon with sales and distribution resuming in the second quarter of 1997.
"Generally, the impact has been worse than we thought at the end of last year," she said.
Centeon LCC in October recalled its Albumin and Plasma Plex products as a precaution against bacterial infection after some vials of the products had shown cracks during transit.
In January, Rhone-Poulenc said that the Centeon problems had cost 0.64 francs on the 1996 earnings per share figure, which was up 25.8 percent to 8.44 francs.
